rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: Finding A asks for the global module-singleton patch to be scoped/documented/restored on dispose; Finding B asks for a missing vim-keymap test exercising the routing. Adding a test leaves the unrestored global patch, and scoping the patch leaves the coverage gap — same mechanism, different defects.

panel.finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts::`routevimhistorytostore()` permanently monkey-patches the shared `@replit/codemirror-vim` module singleton for the whole process
panel.summary: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` permanently monkey-patches the shared `@replit/codemirror-vim` module singleton for the whole process
panel.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:41-58 overwrites `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` on the module-level singleton the first time any note editor mounts, and never restores it on `dispose()`. I grepped the repo for other `@replit/codemirror-vim` importers and found only packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:5 (plus package.json/lockfile), so nothing is broken today — but any future vim-enabled CodeMirror surface in the frontend inherits notes' routing (falling back only when `noteStoreFacet` is absent). Worth a comment/ownership note or a facet-scoped extension instead of a global patch.

coderabbit.evidence: **Add vim-mode coverage for `routeVimHistoryToStore`.** This block tests default-keymap history bindings (Mod-z / Mod-Shift-z). No test in the diff exercises `editor.ts`'s `routeVimHistoryToStore`, which routes vim's `u` / `<C-r>` to the store by monkey-patching `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`. This is new, module-scoped routing logic; a regression there would go undetected. Add a test that switches the editor to `vim` keymap and dispatches `u` / `<C-r>` (or calls `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` directly against the mounted view's `CodeMirror` instance) to confirm it reaches `store.undo()` / `store.redo()`.
